content: Indinavir increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and adjust the dosage as needed based on adverse reactions. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Indinavir is a strong CYP3A inhibitor, and co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates should be avoided. Close monitoring is required. Indinavir decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing the formation of its active alkylating metabolites and decreasing its efficacy. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone also increases indinavir levels through time-dependent CYP3A inhibition, potentially leading to elevated plasma levels of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. Close monitoring is required. Indinavir decreases the effects of insulin aspart due to pharmacodynamic antagonism, potentially causing hyperglycemia through insulin resistance. Use caution, monitor closely, and modify therapy as needed. HIV protease inhibitors, including indinavir, may cause new-onset diabetes mellitus, exacerbate existing diabetes, or cause hyperglycemia. Indinavir decreases the effects of insulin degludec through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. HIV protease inhibitors may induce insulin resistance, leading to hyperglycemia. Indinavir decreases the effects of insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, inhaled insulin, insulin lispro, insulin NPH, and regular human insulin due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Use caution, monitor closely, and consider therapy adjustments. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of irinotecan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity, leading to decreased metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, and alternative drugs should be used. UGT1A1 inhibitors also decrease irinotecan metabolism. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of irinotecan liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity, leading to decreased metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, and alternative drugs should be used. UGT1A1 inhibitors also decrease irinotecan metabolism. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of isradipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Close monitoring is required. Do not exceed 20 mg/day of istradefylline when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Indinavir dosage should be reduced to 600 mg every 8 hours when co-administered with itraconazole. Close monitoring is required. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Ivacaftor increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Indinavir also increases ivacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ivacaftor dosage should be reduced when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Close monitoring is required. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of ivermectin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided, or alternative therapies should be used. If unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. If the strong inhibitor is discontinued, increase the ivosidenib dose to the recommended 500 mg daily after at least five half-lives of the inhibitor. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir decreases the levels or effects of ketamine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Indinavir also increases ketoconazole levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Indinavir increases the levels of lacosamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Close monitoring is required. Indinavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Indinavir also increases lansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Lapatinib also increases indinavir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided, or the larotrectinib dose should be reduced by 50%. Resume the prior larotrectinib dose once the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued for 3-5 half-lives. Lasmiditan increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of leniolisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Indinavir increases the levels of letermovir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Letermovir also increases indinavir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors may require dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine the need for dose adjustment. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Indinavir also increases levoketoconazole levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Indinavir interacts with oral contraceptives containing levonorgestrel, ethinyl estradiol, and ferrous bisglycinate, potentially causing significant changes in estrogen plasma levels and reducing contraceptive efficacy. Use a nonhormonal contraceptive method. Indinavir decreases the effects of linagliptin and liraglutide due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Lomitapide also increases indinavir levels. Consider reducing the dose when used concomitantly. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir also increases indinavir levels. Use caution and monitor closely.
